On 2026-05-11, the billing importer retried failed Stripe events for 47 minutes after the queue worker lost its lease. Three merchants received duplicate invoice emails, two refunds were delayed until support reran the reconciliation job, and no card was charged twice.

Worker logs show lease-renewal failures from 09:14 to 10:01 UTC. The team disabled retries at 10:07 UTC, replayed the affected events from a frozen export, and added a guard that blocks retry fan-out when lease renewal fails. That guard shipped behind the BillingLeaseGuard feature flag on 2026-05-12.

The affected invoices were reviewed, and the specific retry fan-out path is now blocked. One limitation remains: exports created before 2026-04-01 do not include merchant timezone, so the replay tool still requires manual review for that subset.

Contractors may request read-only production access only when the incident commander records a Sev1 or Sev2 incident. A manager cannot approve the request alone. Security must approve it in AccessDesk, and access expires after 24 hours.

Contractors cannot export customer data, cannot run write queries, and cannot use shared accounts. The only exception is that the on-call database administrator may extend access once for 12 hours if the incident remains open and Security records the extension before the first grant expires.

The policy owner is Security Operations. The next review date is 2026-07-01.

We spent 18 months building AtlasLedger for accountants who still reconcile SaaS invoices in spreadsheets. The first version tried to classify every contract term, and it failed.

The version that worked is narrow on purpose. It imports invoice PDFs, matches line items against the renewal table, and flags discounts that disappear after the first year. Eight firms used the private beta. Five kept using it after the trial.

The best feedback was small: junior staff stopped copying renewal dates by hand on Fridays. That is the product.

We observed 42 remote design critiques across 11 product teams from January 2026 to March 2026. The teams used the same review template but different facilitation rules. The only consistent pattern was that critiques with a named decision owner closed more comments within 72 hours.

This observation does not show that templates cause better decisions, and it does not generalize to engineering reviews.

If it still fails, send the import ID from the error panel.
